name: free-african-society-founded
description: Richard Allen and Absalom Jones led Black Philadelphians in forming a mutual aid society for self-help and dignity.

name: walkers-appeal-pamphlet
description: A Boston clothier printed a fiery pamphlet urging Black Americans to resist oppression and demand their rights.

name: crandall-school-black-girls
description: A Connecticut teacher took Black girls into her academy, provoking a boycott and laws meant to close the school.

name: fourteenth-amendment-ratified
description: A constitutional amendment promised citizenship and equal protection of the laws to all born in the country, freed Black Americans included.

name: fifteenth-amendment-ratified
description: An amendment barred denying the vote on grounds of race, giving Black men the franchise on paper.

name: wells-southern-horrors
description: A Memphis journalist used careful reporting to expose the myths excusing mob violence and began a campaign against lynching.

name: gandhi-thrown-off-train
description: A young lawyer with a first-class ticket was ejected at a South African station for his skin colour, sparking his resistance.

name: du-bois-souls-black-folk
friendly_name: Du Bois's Souls of Black Folk
description: A scholar's essays on the colour line challenged accommodation and demanded full civil rights for Black Americans.

name: garvey-founds-unia
description: Marcus Garvey launched a Jamaican organisation promoting Black pride, self-reliance and unity across the African diaspora.

name: first-pan-african-congress-paris
description: Black leaders from Africa, the Caribbean and America met alongside the post-war peace talks to press for equality and colonial reform.

name: pullman-porters-union
description: A. Philip Randolph organised Black sleeping-car workers into a union that later powered national civil rights protests.

name: executive-order-8802
description: Facing a threatened mass march on the capital, the president ordered an end to racial discrimination in war industries.

name: truman-desegregates-military
description: An executive order declared equal treatment for all service members regardless of race, ending formal segregation in the armed forces.

name: mlk-day-signed
description: The president signed a bill creating a national holiday honouring the slain civil rights leader after a long campaign.

name: tutu-nobel-peace-prize
friendly_name: Tutu Wins the Nobel Peace Prize
description: The Anglican archbishop was honoured for his peaceful opposition to apartheid, bringing the cause fresh world attention.
